body: Deploying Product Forge SaaS or Enterprise editions currently requires executing multiple manual steps (database migration, object store setup, environment configuration, service runner startup). A turnkey enterprise product requires an automated one-command infrastructure-as-code deployment pipeline. This item provides the official Helm chart and Terraform modules.
_note: Full authoring of context, epic, and ACs

brief.problem: Plane A (Product Forge platform itself) lacks an automated turnkey one-click cloud provisioning bundle (Helm chart + Terraform), requiring manual database and cluster configuration.
brief.what_adds: Plane A One-Click Cloud Provisioner: Helm chart and Terraform modules for automated Product Forge cluster deployment.

design_pack.title: Plane A One-Click Cloud Provisioner: Helm chart and Terraform modules for automated Product Forge cluster deployment

quotas.cloud_resources: Configurable node pools and database instance classes matching environment sizing

rollout: Rolling update deployment strategy with zero downtime maxSurge: 1, maxUnavailable: 0.

controls.control: Helm chart deploys complete Product Forge platform stack including PostgreSQL with pgvector, object store, and core API pods
Terraform module automates cloud VPC, managed Kubernetes cluster, and HA database provisioning across AWS and GCP
Database credentials and API tokens managed via Kubernetes Secrets with non-root pod security contexts
Multi-tenant database schema initialization with pgvector extension and tenant RLS isolation
Non-destructive rollback triggered when post-deployment health check probes fail or timeout
Single command deployment script provisions infrastructure, deploys Helm chart, and passes automated post-deploy health check

rollback: Non-destructive helm rollback to prior healthy revision; teardown requires explicit confirmation.
security: Database credentials and tokens stored in Kubernetes Secrets, never plaintext in values.
Container securityContext enforces runAsNonRoot and readOnlyRootFilesystem.

db: PostgreSQL 15+ with pgvector extension enabled; S3-compatible object store.
api: Existing GET /api/v1/health and GET /healthz system probes; no new routes required.
config: Helm values.yaml and Terraform variables.tf with parameterized region, cluster size, and db tier.

decisions: Standalone decoupled root modules for AWS and GCP to eliminate credential cross-coupling.
PVC reclaimPolicy Retain to guarantee zero accidental database loss.
learnings: Coupled multi-cloud Terraform modules cause spurious credential errors; keep root modules strictly provider-isolated.
non_goals: Plane B client application deployments (handled in core/deploy_providers.py)
Public DNS domain delegation or commercial TLS certificate management (pluggable via cert-manager)

data_model.schema: PostgreSQL 15+ relational schema with pgvector extension and multi-tenant RLS policies

guardrails: Data loss prevention guardrail: retain PVCs on rollback and teardown.
Realistic SLA guardrail: 10m warm / 25m cold cluster bounds.
invariants: Provisioning is idempotent: rerunning with identical parameters creates zero duplicate resources.
Non-destructive rollback: rollbacks execute helm rollback to prior healthy revision without destroying database state.
Persistent volume protection: PVCs enforce reclaimPolicy: Retain.
Multi-AZ HA database: cloud deployments provision Multi-AZ managed databases with automated failover.
Dry-run validation: provisioner supports --dry-run and --plan without making cloud changes.
Health-gated completion: deployment verified with /api/v1/health probe in under 10m warm / 25m cold.

proof_plan.red_evidence: Missing chart templates or invalid Terraform syntax causes contract test failure; unreachable health probe triggers timeout.
proof_plan.green_evidence: Helm template renders cleanly; Terraform validates; deployer passes health verification in under SLA.

rls_tenant.reason: PostgreSQL database initialized with tenant isolation schemas and pgvector vector search tables

performance: Warm cluster deployment SLA under 10 minutes.
Cold cloud infrastructure provisioning SLA under 25 minutes.

api_contract.validation: returns status ok and database connectivity check

dependencies: BI-PF-1309: Multi-tenant PostgreSQL database with pgvector

design_areas.reason: Turnkey Helm chart, multi-cloud Terraform modules, and one-click deployment runner

requirements: AC-1: Helm chart deploys complete Product Forge platform stack including PostgreSQL with pgvector, object store, and core API pods with persistent volume retention.
AC-2: Terraform module automates cloud VPC, managed Kubernetes cluster, and HA database provisioning across AWS and GCP providers.

AC-3: Single command deployment script provisions infrastructure, deploys Helm chart, and passes automated post-deploy health check in under 10 minutes on warm clusters (25 minutes for cold cloud cluster provisioning), with dry-run support.
design_pack.compatibility: Compatible with standard cloud-managed Kubernetes v1.28+ and PostgreSQL 15+
observability: Structured deployment logging with timestamps, phase markers, and exit codes.
Prometheus scraping annotations on service endpoints.
design_pack.backup_restore: Pre-flight snapshot verification required; PVCs configured with reclaimPolicy Retain to prevent accidental storage loss

failure_matrix.expected: pod probe fails and deployment aborts
fail closed and report diagnostic logs

security_model.confidentiality: Database credentials, secrets, and API tokens stored in Kubernetes Secrets with non-root securityContext

stop_conditions: Any precheck gate failure or test regression halts delivery.

failure_taxonomy.handling: fail closed and trigger non-destructive rollback

runtime_contract.contract: Inputs: provider, config, dry-run -> Output: provisioned cluster and healthy platform
runtime_contract.failure_behavior: Fail fast, output diagnostics, exit with code 1

design_pack.rollback_recovery: Non-destructive rollback via helm rollback <release> <revision> to reinstate prior known-good platform pods without destroying database state
design_pack.deployment_rollout: Kubernetes rolling update strategy with maxSurge: 1 and maxUnavailable: 0 for zero-downtime platform upgrades

performance_capacity.latency_target: under 10 minutes on warm cluster; under 25 minutes for cold cloud cluster provisioning

concurrency_idempotency.concurrency: Single deployer lock prevents overlapping cluster mutation
concurrency_idempotency.idempotency: Declarative Terraform and Helm state ensures identical runs produce zero duplicate resources

Terraform module automates cloud VPC, managed Kubernetes cluster, and HA database provisioning across AWS and GCP
Database credentials and API tokens managed via Kubernetes Secrets with non-root pod security contexts

tier_reasons: Plane A turnkey infrastructure provisioning and deployment automation
verification: End-to-end deployment test executing one_click_deploy.sh on test cluster and verifying healthy status endpoint.

NIT: Ensure `core/deploy_providers.py` edits are limited to infrastructure orchestration tooling rather than adding core platform runtime logic in Python (Language Rule).
MAJOR: AC-3 SLA of under 10 minutes for cloud VPC, managed EKS/GKE cluster, database provisioning, and platform deployment is architecturally unrealistic and will lead to deterministic deployment timeout failures.
Production Helm stack deploys single-instance PostgreSQL and MinIO subcharts without multi-AZ HA replication, failover strategy, or external secret management integration (Guardrail 2).
MINOR: `one_click_deploy.sh` lacks explicit dry-run (`terraform plan`) validation modes and target environment confirmation boundaries prior to resource provisioning (Guardrail 4).
BLOCKER: Rollback design specifies destructive `terraform destroy` / `helm uninstall` teardown without pre-destroy backup verifications or persistent volume retention policies, risking irrecoverable data loss (Guardrail 1).
SUMMARY: Design cannot be approved due to data loss risks during automated teardown and an unachievable provisioning SLA.
Primary risks include catastrophic storage destruction upon rollback and false-negative deployment failures from cloud infrastructure creation latency.

acceptance_criteria: AC-1: Helm chart deploys complete Product Forge platform stack including PostgreSQL with pgvector, object store, and core API pods.
AC-2: Terraform module automates cloud VPC, managed Kubernetes cluster, and database provisioning across AWS and GCP providers.
AC-3: Single command deployment script provisions infrastructure, deploys Helm chart, and passes automated post-deploy health check in under 10 minutes.
